wards.name: CHD-WARD-01
wards.description: A relatively established urban ward with a mixture of residential areas and open spaces. Moderate wind flow and vegetation provide some relief from thermal stress, although exposed built-up areas may experience higher afternoon temperatures.

wards.name: CHD-WARD-02
wards.description: A mixed residential and urban region with moderate built-up density. Heat exposure can increase during sunny afternoon periods, particularly in areas with limited shade.

wards.name: CHD-WARD-03
wards.description: A predominantly urban region with moderate vegetation and built-up surfaces. Reduced wind movement during hot periods can increase perceived thermal stress.

wards.name: CHD-WARD-04
wards.description: A moderately dense urban ward where solar exposure and relatively low wind speeds can contribute to increased heat stress during peak afternoon hours.

wards.name: CHD-WARD-05
wards.description: A mixed-use region with moderate-to-high thermal exposure. Lower wind speeds combined with elevated humidity can make outdoor conditions uncomfortable during prolonged heat events.

wards.name: CHD-WARD-08
wards.description: An urban ward with a combination of residential and open areas. Moderate vegetation provides partial protection, while exposed paved areas can accumulate heat.

wards.name: CHD-WARD-09
wards.description: A moderately built-up region with reasonable airflow. Thermal stress is expected to remain moderate under normal conditions but can increase during prolonged hot weather.

wards.name: CHD-WARD-10
wards.description: A mixed urban region with moderate solar exposure. Reduced wind movement and high afternoon radiation can increase heat accumulation in built-up locations.

wards.name: CHD-WARD-11
wards.description: A comparatively open region with better airflow and moderate vegetation. These characteristics can reduce thermal stress compared with more densely built-up wards.

wards.name: CHD-WARD-12
wards.description: A mixed urban region with moderate vegetation and built-up surfaces. Thermal conditions can become uncomfortable during periods of high solar radiation.

wards.name: CHD-WARD-13
wards.description: A moderately dense urban ward where heat exposure varies between shaded and highly exposed areas. Reduced wind speeds can increase thermal discomfort.

wards.name: CHD-WARD-14
wards.description: A relatively compact urban region with moderate heat exposure. Adequate airflow can provide some mitigation, although direct solar exposure remains important.

wards.name: CHD-WARD-15
wards.description: A moderately-to-highly exposed urban region. Combination of elevated temperature, humidity and lower wind speeds can result in increased human thermal stress.

wards.name: CHD-WARD-16
wards.description: A mixed urban ward with moderate built-up density. Heat stress may increase during afternoon periods when solar radiation is high and wind movement is limited.

wards.name: CHD-WARD-17
wards.description: A predominantly urban region with moderate-to-high heat exposure. Prolonged outdoor activity during hot periods may result in elevated thermal stress.

wards.name: CHD-WARD-18
wards.description: A densely developed region where reduced wind movement and high solar exposure can contribute to significant heat accumulation. Vulnerable groups may require additional protection during heat events.

wards.name: CHD-WARD-19
wards.description: An urban region with moderate-to-high thermal exposure. Elevated humidity combined with low wind speeds can increase perceived heat stress.

wards.name: CHD-WARD-20
wards.description: A relatively exposed urban ward where high solar radiation and limited wind movement can increase thermal stress during hot afternoons.

wards.name: CHD-WARD-21
wards.description: A mixed urban region with moderate thermal exposure. Heat conditions can vary considerably depending on local shade, vegetation and built-up surfaces.

wards.name: CHD-WARD-22
wards.description: A region with relatively better airflow and moderate thermal exposure. Outdoor conditions are generally less stressful than highly built-up areas under the same weather conditions.

wards.name: CHD-WARD-25
wards.description: A highly urbanized region with relatively high thermal exposure. Elevated humidity, low wind speed and strong solar radiation can combine to produce significant human thermal stress during heat events.
